title: Lumio SaaS Support POC
summary: Enterprise SaaS support POC for Lumio — 3 capabilities, 3 features, 12 seeded tickets, 8 KB articles, Slack + feature_request_handler integrations, and an Enterprise SLA policy.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Prerequisites — verify before running setup steps
steps: Confirm the DevRev user behind your PAT has the Admin role. Builder/Member roles cannot reach all Settings menus, and several integrations require Admin to install snap-ins.
Confirm the PAT itself was generated by that same Admin user. PATs inherit the creator's role at the moment they were issued — escalating the user later does NOT re-scope existing tokens.
If a step below returns an 'access required' or HTTP 403 error, regenerate the PAT from an Admin account and rerun `dia doctor` before retrying.
Some Settings menus are scoped per-workspace; confirm you're operating in the workspace the customer will use, not your default DevRev org.

ui_guidance_sections.title: SLA Policy Setup
steps: Navigate to Settings → Support → SLA Policies.
Create a new policy named 'Lumio Enterprise SLA'.
Set First Response targets: P0=30 min, P1=2 h, P2=8 h, P3=24 h.
Set Resolution targets: P0=4 h, P1=24 h, P2=72 h, P3=168 h (1 week).
Add escalation rule: page on-call if P0 first response is not met within 15 min; escalate P1 to team lead after 1 h.
Apply this policy to tickets tagged with account tier 'Enterprise'.
Reference: https://devrev.ai/docs/DevRevU/demos

ui_guidance_sections.title: Slack Integration
steps: Navigate to Settings → Integrations → Slack.
Authorise the DevRev Slack app in your workspace.
Map a Slack channel (e.g. #lumio-support-alerts) to receive ticket notifications.
Enable bi-directional sync so Slack thread replies appear as timeline entries in DevRev.
Reference: https://developer.devrev.ai/beta/about/for-developers

ui_guidance_sections.title: Feature Request Handler (Auto-promote tickets to enhancements)
steps: Navigate to Settings → Snap-ins → Feature Request Handler.
Install the snap-in and configure the trigger keyword (e.g. 'feature request' or 'enhancement').
Set the target part to 'Lumio Platform' or a specific capability so promoted items land in the right part of the hierarchy.
Configure the Slack notification to post to #lumio-product-feedback when a ticket is promoted.
Reference: https://devrev.ai/docs/DevRevU/demos

ui_guidance_sections.title: PLuG Chat Widget Deployment
steps: Navigate to Settings → PLuG → Widget.
Set the welcome message: 'Hi! I'm the Lumio Support Assistant. Ask me anything about authentication, billing, or integrations.'
Set primary colour to #6C47FF.
Enable AI Agent and set fallback action to 'Create ticket'.
Under AI Grounding, select all 8 published KB articles as source material.
Copy the embed snippet and add it to the Lumio web app's <head>.
Reference: https://developer.devrev.ai/beta/about/for-developers

ui_guidance_sections.title: Saved Views for Demo
steps: Create a 'P0 & P1 Open Tickets' view filtered by severity IN [high] AND status != closed.
Create a 'Tickets by Capability' view grouped by applies_to_part for a visual breakdown across Auth, Billing, and Integrations.
Pin both views to the left nav for fast access during the demo walkthrough.
Reference: https://devrev.ai/docs/DevRevU/demos

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure SLA policies
steps: Settings → SLA Policies → Create
Recreate each policy below, matching the priority targets exactly.
Policy: Lumio Enterprise SLA (applies to tickets with account tier: Enterprise)
Notes: Enterprise-tier SLA for Lumio customers with aggressive first-response and resolution targets.
First-response: p0 (blocker) ≤ 30m, p1 (high) ≤ 2h, p2 (medium) ≤ 8h, p3 (low) ≤ 24h
Resolution: p0 (blocker) ≤ 4h, p1 (high) ≤ 24h, p2 (medium) ≤ 72h, p3 (low) ≤ 168h
Escalation: Page on-call engineer if P0 first response is not met within 15 minutes. Escalate P1 to team lead after 1 hour.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Deploy the PLuG chat widget
steps: Settings → PLuG → Widget
Copy the JavaScript snippet and add it to your site's <head> (or deploy via GTM).
Set welcome message: "Hi! I'm the Lumio Support Assistant. Ask me anything about authentication, billing, or integrations."
Set primary brand color: #6C47FF
Enable the AI agent for L1 deflection.
Ground the AI on the KB articles seeded by this blueprint (Settings → AI Agent → Sources).
Notes: Ground AI agent on the 8 published KB articles covering SSO setup, MFA recovery, billing/invoices, plan upgrades, webhooks, API rate limits, IdP group sync, and OAuth token troubleshooting.
Enable fallback to ticket creation when the AI cannot resolve.

Customer-portal auth limitation: the customer-facing portal does NOT support federated login (SAML / OIDC). End users authenticate via email + magic-link only. Surface this early in the POV if the customer is expecting SSO for their end users.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure Slack integration
steps: Settings → Integrations → Slack
Click 'Connect Slack Workspace' and authorize DevRev in the OAuth flow.
Choose a default channel for ticket-event notifications.
Enable bidirectional sync between Slack threads and ticket timelines.
Set up the /devrev slash command for in-Slack ticket creation.
Constraints to flag with the customer up front:
- Only ONE public Slack connection per DevRev org. If they have multiple Slack workspaces, pick the one the support team uses for the POV.
- Enterprise Slack accounts require DevRev Support to whitelist the OAuth app before the install will succeed. File the request with Support ahead of the demo if the customer is on Enterprise Grid.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Install the Feature Request Handler snap-in
steps: Settings → Integrations → Snap-ins → Marketplace
Search for 'Feature Request Handler' and install it.
Configure the trigger stage on tickets that should auto-promote to enhancements (typically 'accepted' or 'work in progress').
Map the source-ticket part → target-enhancement part. The default behavior creates the enhancement under the same part as the ticket; override per part if your customer wants a separate roadmap area.
Pick the visibility for the auto-created enhancement (internal vs customer-visible). Most POVs want internal until the workflow is proven.
Test by transitioning one ticket into the trigger stage and confirm an enhancement is created and linked back via the timeline.
